title: Light-Induced Dielectrophoresis for Characterizing the Electrical Behavior of Human Mesenchymal Stem Cells
protocol: Clean the ITO-coated glass substrate by flowing nitrogen gas at a flow rate sufficient to move visible dust particles.
Rinse the substrate with acetone.
Transfer the ITO-coated glass slide to an isopropyl alcohol bath and rinse with DI water.
Flow N2 gas until the substrate is completely dry.
Place the glass slide with the ITO-coated side up into the vacuum sputtering system.
Sputter a 10 nm thick layer of molybdenum onto the ITO-coated glass substrate with a deposition rate of 0.7 Å/s and a deposition time of 140 s.
Add a shadow mask to one side of the glass substrate to leave 2 mm from the edge uncovered for electrical connections.
Deposit 1 µm of A:Si using inductively coupled plasma-plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition (ICP-PECVD).
Clean the slide with N2 gas to remove dust and other impurities.
Submerge the edge up to the 2 mm mark in a 25% w/v potassium hydroxide solution to etch the A:Si.
Obtain double-sided tape (52 mm x 25 mm) and punch holes (diameter = 4 mm) 5-6 mm away from the edge of the shorter dimension and centered between the longer sides of the tape.
Cut two straight lines (3 mm apart) across the holes using a scalpel.
Drill two 3 mm diameter holes in the top ITO glass slide.
Mark the hole location with a washable marker on the ITO-coated glass.
Align the drilled holes with the holes punched in the double-sided tape.
Remove one side of the protective film on the double-sided tape and align it with the top ITO glass slide.
Press the tape and ITO glass together gently to remove air pockets near the microchannel.
Remove the other protective film from the double-sided tape and press onto the molybdenum and A:Si-coated ITO glass side.
Match the edge of the photoconductive slide opposite the 2 mm clearance side with the edge of the double-sided tape toward the center of the top ITO glass slide.
Press on a flat surface to ensure good adhesion.
Cut off excess tape on the side.
Apply copper tape to the edges of layer A and layer C to connect the function generator.
Wrap the tape from the edge of the double-sided tape to about 3 cm onto the uncoated side of the glass substrate, depending if it is layer A or layer C.
Use a multimeter to test for resistance between coated slides of both glass substrates and copper tape attached to the glass.
Measure out 4.25 g of sucrose and place into a 50 mL conical tube.
Measure out 0.15 g of glucose and place into the same 50 mL conical tube.
Fill the conical tube with 25 mL of ultrapure water.
Close the lid and mix until half of the sucrose and glucose have dissolved.
Add ultrapure water to fill the conical tube up to the 50 mL line.
Mix vigorously until all sucrose and glucose are dissolved.
Obtain 20 mL of the prepared sucrose and glucose solution.
Place the obtained solution into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Measure out 0.1 g of bovine serum albumin (BSA).
Add BSA to the 50 mL conical tube containing the sucrose and glucose solution.
Vortex until the BSA is completely dissolved.
Obtain at least 1 x 10^6 cells suspended in 1 mL of growth medium.
Place the cell suspension into a 10 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge HEK 293 cells at 201 x g for 5 min.
Centrifuge hMSCs at 290 x g for 10 min.
Aspirate the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of DEP buffer solution containing 0.5% BSA.
Avoid adding the buffer too quickly to prevent bubble formation.
Repeat the centrifugation process two more times.
Resuspend cells in DEP buffer with 0.5% BSA for LiDEP characterization.
Assemble a laptop, projector, objective lens, digital microscope, and function generator for experimental setup.
Design light projections (star, diamond, three lines, oval) on the laptop.
Connect the laptop to the projector.
Display light projections from the projector onto the photoconductive surface of the LiDEP chip using a 10x objective lens.
Connect the LiDEP chip to the function generator.
Observe cells experiencing the LiDEP force with the digital microscope for imaging and video recording.
Flush the microchannel with 70% ethanol.
Flush the microchannel again with 0.5% BSA solution two more times.
Remove the 0.5% BSA solution with a pipette.
Fit the microfluidic device into the device holder.
Attach alligator clips to each of the copper tape connections on the device.
Set the function generator to the desired voltage (Vpp) and frequency (Hz).
Add 70 µL of cell suspension (cells + DEP buffer solution with 0.5% BSA) into the device microchannel.
Tilt the pipette tip slightly in the hole toward the microchannel to reduce spillage.
Wipe away any access solution (0.5% BSA or cells in solution) with single-use paper wipes and discard them into biohazard waste.
Project the desired virtual electrode geometry onto the LiDEP chip.
Set the video length to 3 min in the digital microscope software.
Set a lab timer to 2 min 30 s.
Once cells are stationary, press Start in the digital microscope software to begin recording.
Wait 10 s, then press the ON button of the function generator channel output to apply the AC electric field.
Press Start for the timer and monitor cell DEP behavior through the digital microscope.
Prevent shaking or movement around the setup during the experiment.
Once the timer goes off, press the ON button of the function generator channel output to turn it off.
Stop the video recording at 3 min and save it for future analysis.
Pipette cells out of the outlet end of the LiDEP chip by slowly pushing 60 µL of DEP buffer with 0.5% BSA into the microchannel.
Simultaneously collect the contents at the outlet until there are little to no cells in the microchannel.
Repeat steps from projecting virtual electrode geometry through collecting remaining cells for all frequencies tested.
